answer.summary: For a linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors tested against R² = 0 (omnibus F-test), with 80 participants, anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30, and significance level α = 0.05 (one-sided), the noncentral F-test power is 0.624.
answer.method: Noncentral F-distribution. The test statistic F = [R²/k] / [(1−R²)/(n−k−1)] follows a central F(k, n−k−1) distribution under H₀. Under H₁, it follows a noncentral F distribution with noncentrality parameter λ = n·R²/(1−R²). Power is computed as P(F > F_crit) where F_crit is the upper α quantile of the central F(k, n−k−1) distribution, evaluated under the noncentral F distribution with the specified λ. Here k=3 predictors, n=80 participants, R²=(0.30)²=0.09, df_num=3, df_den=76, λ=7.912.
assumptions: Linear regression model correctly specified with intercept and 3 fixed predictors
Residuals are normally distributed with homogeneous variance
No multicollinearity interfering with F-test validity
One-sided test: H₀: R² = 0 vs H₁: R² > 0
limitations: Power estimate depends on the assumed population multiple correlation of 0.30; other effect sizes will yield different power
No allowance made for model misspecification, missing assumptions, or violations of linearity and homogeneity
Design assumes complete data and no attrition
Power reflects the omnibus test of all 3 predictors; does not address planned contrast or individual predictor tests

# Power calculation for R-squared test in linear regression
# H0: R^2 = 0 vs H1: R^2 > 0

# Parameters
n <- 80                          # Sample size
rho <- 0.30                      # Multiple correlation coefficient
k <- 3                           # Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
alpha <- 0.05                    # Significance level

# Degrees of freedom
df_num <- k                      # Numerator df = number of predictors
df_den <- n - k - 1             # Denominator df = n - k - 1

# Convert multiple correlation to R-squared
R2 <- rho^2

# Noncentrality parameter lambda for F-distribution
# lambda = n * R^2 / (1 - R^2)
lambda <- n * R2 / (1 - R2)

# Critical F-value from central F distribution at alpha = 0.05
critical_F <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_den)

# Power = P(F > critical_F) under noncentral F distribution with noncentrality lambda
# Using pf with ncp parameter
power <- 1 - pf(critical_F, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)

# Summary output
cat("=== Linear Regression R-squared Power Calculation ===\n")
cat("Sample size (n):", n, "participants\n")
cat("Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("R-squared:", R2, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("\n--- Degrees of Freedom ---\n")
cat("Numerator df (k):", df_num, "\n")
cat("Denominator df (n - k - 1):", df_den, "\n")
cat("\n--- Test Calculation ---\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", lambda, "\n")
cat("Critical F-value F(", df_num, ",", df_den, ",", alpha, "):", critical_F, "\n")
cat("Power (1 - sided, α = 0.05):", power, "\n")

# Return structured result
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", results_json, "\n", sep = "")
